article.headline: Nobody's Googling you anymore
article.description: Issue #1 of The AI Collective Weekly: why customers are asking ChatGPT instead of Google, and the one thing every Prairie business should do this week.

runs.text: Morning. Welcome to the first issue of The AI Collective Weekly.
One email, every Thursday. Plain English, no hype, and something you can actually use before the coffee's cold. Here's the deal for issue #1.
A customer used to find you one way: they'd type "plumber Regina" into Google and scroll. Simple, and for twenty years, SEO was the whole game.
That's quietly changing. More people — especially anyone under 40 — now open ChatGPT, Google's AI overview, or their phone's assistant and just
ask
: "Who's a good plumber in Regina that does emergency calls?" And the AI gives them one answer. Not a page of ten links. One recommendation, maybe three.
If your business isn't in that answer, you don't exist for that customer. There's no page two to fight for anymore. There's the answer, or there's silence.

blocks.heading: Why this matters more on the Prairies

runs.text: Here's the good news, and it's real: most local businesses in Saskatchewan haven't figured this out yet. The big national chains are optimizing hard for AI search. Your competitor down the street almost certainly isn't. That's a window — and windows close.

Being the business AI recommends when someone asks isn't luck. It's a handful of specific, boring, do-it-once things: making sure your business facts are consistent everywhere online, having real reviews, and publishing plain answers to the questions customers actually ask. We call it AEO — Answer Engine Optimization. It's the new SEO, and it's very learnable.
Open ChatGPT (or Google's AI) and ask it, as a customer would:
"Who are the best [what you do] in [your town]?"
Then ask a follow-up:
"Tell me more about [your business name]."
Write down what it says. Is your business mentioned at all? Is what it says
right
— hours, services, location? For most owners, this first look is a gut-check. If you're missing or the details are wrong, that's exactly what we'll help you fix.
This week's anchor guide walks through the exact checklist a Saskatoon contractor used to get named in AI answers within six weeks — schema, profiles, reviews, and content, step by step.
Read: Get cited by ChatGPT & AI search →

That's it for issue #1. Next Thursday: the five repetitive tasks quietly eating your Mondays, and how to hand most of them to AI. If a business friend would find this useful, forward it — that's how a Prairie thing grows.
— The AI Collective, Saskatchewan
